mentions.name: Marmot
mentions.description: Marmot is a database project that recently added support for vector indexing. After implementing a research paper indexing algorithm, the author tuned it for their own use case, resulting in a replicatable RAG store; local benchmarks show decent QPS with under a GB of RSS on the DBpedia dataset.
mentions.problem: The initial implementation of the research paper indexing algorithm did not perform well enough, requiring tuning for the author's use case.
mentions.source_excerpt: Working on Marmot https://github.com/maxpert/marmot recently added support for vector index. My local benchmarks show pretty decent QPS with less than GB of RSS on DBpedia dataset.

mentions.name: Marmot
mentions.description: Distributed database replication project that now has replicas working with a DML proxy, allowing a cluster of primaries and read-only replicas spun up on demand; nodes talking to localhost never see their mutations served transparently from read-only replicas. A proof of concept works, though snapshot restore is still extremely inefficient.
mentions.problem: Snapshot restore is currently extremely inefficient, despite the proof of concept working.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I am as usual working on Marmot https://github.com/maxpert/marmot

I've got replicas now working with DML proxy. This essentially means I can now have a cluster of primaries, and then spin up replicas on demand and nodes talking to local host will never see their mutation work pretty transparently from readonly-replicas.
